entries.title: Kāma
entries.tension: renunciation is causal risk-management, not mere moral prohibition

entries.title: Guhaṭṭhaka
entries.tension: body language must not be collapsed into body-hatred

entries.title: Duṭṭhaṭṭhaka
moves: sage not defined by polemical status

entries.title: Suddhaṭṭhaka
moves: sage does not seize one highest identity
release not reducible to conceptual badge
entries.tension: knowledge remains instrumental but not an identity-possession

entries.title: Paramaṭṭhaka
entries.tension: must reconcile with right view function

entries.title: Jarā
entries.tension: de-appropriation is practical response to mortality

entries.title: Tissametteyya
entries.tension: specific renunciant discipline, not universal lay prescription

entries.title: Pasūra
entries.tension: truth-seeking must be separated from debate-as-identity

entries.title: Māgaṇḍiya
moves: purity not by view/learning/knowledge/ritual nor their simple absence
entries.tension: anti-binary purification language is easy to mistranslate as anti-knowledge

entries.title: Purābheda
entries.tension: sage profile supplements, not replaces, formal path lists

entries.title: Cūḷabyūha
moves: one truth vs many proclaimed truths
sage does not build identity on verdict

entries.title: Mahābyūha
moves: praise gained in debate is small
do not take seen/heard/thought as identity basis
entries.tension: non-dispute must not erase ethical correction

entries.title: Tuvaṭaka
moves: request for rapid path to peace
entries.tension: chapter is not merely anti-doctrinal; it contains positive training

entries.title: Attadaṇḍa
entries.tension: social violence analysis joins inward craving analysis

entries.title: Sāriputta
entries.tension: concrete discipline closes the vagga and guards against nihilistic anti-rule readings

cross_cutting_result: The chapter attacks appropriation, comparison and contest around desire/views/purity, while retaining positive discipline and a non-relativist concern with truth and release.
next_pass: lexical audit diṭṭhi/sacca/saññā/maññati/papañca/nissaya and northern Arthapada comparison
